title: Account Discovery: Email Account
summary: Email Account discovery collects addresses and mailbox identities, most often by dumping the global address list, the shared directory of everyone in an organisation, from an on-premises mail server or a hosted mail service. The output is a ready-made target list for phishing and for guessing login names on other systems, and it can also expose distribution groups that reveal teams, seniority, and reporting lines. Enumeration needs an authenticated mailbox session, so the query itself is a normal administrative action and the interesting signal is its size and timing: a newly created or recently compromised mailbox pulling the entire address list minutes after its first successful logon. Detection combines mail platform audit records of bulk directory reads with behavioural baselines for how much contact data each mailbox normally exports.

beginner.definition: This is collecting the list of email addresses used by an organisation. Mail systems often keep a shared address book called a global address list. Unlike the parent technique, which covers accounts of every kind, this sub-technique focuses on email addresses and mailboxes. The addresses are not secret, but the full list is useful.
beginner.whyItMatters: An email list is the starting point for a phishing campaign. Attackers use real names and real team addresses to make a fake message look genuine. The list also helps them guess login names for other systems. Because reading the address book is a normal action, it is easy to miss. The clue is when one mailbox reads everything at once, soon after first use.
howItWorks: The attacker signs in to a mailbox or mail administration session with stolen or guessed credentials.
They run a mail command that exports the global address list, the shared company address book.
They collect names, addresses and sometimes job titles or team group names.
They use the results to build a target list for phishing messages.
They may also use the naming pattern to guess logins for other services.
Defenders detect bulk address book exports and address list reads by new accounts.
beginner.example: Picture a post office that keeps a printed list of every resident in town so staff can deliver internal notices. A new clerk copies the whole list on their first morning. Nothing is stolen and the list is not secret, but that clerk can now address a convincing letter to any resident. Email account discovery is that copy of the residents list.
takeaways: Bulk exports of the company address book deserve investigation.
Restrict who can read the full address list.
Watch new mailboxes that read unusually large amounts of data.

objectives: Explain what a global address list is and what it reveals.
Describe how email account discovery supports phishing campaigns.
Identify mail platform logs that record address list access and export.
Explain how this sub-technique differs from local and domain account discovery.
Describe the controls that limit address list exposure.
